q: It refers to the orderly arrangement within a piece of land or property of vertical structures such as buildings, monuments and the like, as well as horizontal developments.
n: Physical planning is the orderly arrangement of vertical structures (buildings, monuments) and horizontal developments within a piece of land. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203, Sec. 7.3 (Physical Planning Services).

q: In subdivision development, the preliminary organization, naming, and division of parcels, blocks, and land uses prior to detailed engineering and infrastructure design are generally undertaken during which stage?
n: Conceptual planning is the early stage that organizes parcels, blocks and land uses before detailed engineering and infrastructure design. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203 (Physical Planning); PD 957 Revised IRR (preliminary approval and locational clearance stage).

q: Which planning activity involves dividing a large parcel of land into individual lots, roads, open spaces, utility corridors, and other development components in preparation for future subdivision development?
n: Subdivision planning divides a large parcel into lots, roads, open spaces and utility corridors in preparation for subdivision development. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR; 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203 (Physical Planning).

q: After the overall subdivision plan has been approved conceptually, which activity is primarily concerned with establishing the precise configuration, dimensions, frontage, depth, and boundaries of individual lots and road rights-of-way for inclusion in the subdivision plan?
n: Subdivision layout and lot delineation fixes the exact configuration, dimensions, frontage, depth and boundaries of each lot and road right-of-way. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (subdivision plan requirements).

q: It entails the formulation of site criteria, assistance to the client in site evaluation, as well as analysis to determine the most appropriate site/s for a proposed project or building program.
n: Site selection and analysis means setting site criteria and helping the client evaluate and analyze sites to find the most appropriate one for the project. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Site Selection and Analysis.

q: During the subdivision planning process, at which phase should the project site be evaluated for its physical characteristics, opportunities, and constraints before any design work begins?
n: A site's physical characteristics, opportunities and constraints are evaluated during site selection and analysis, before any design work. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Site Selection and Analysis.

q: Before any site development work can be properly planned and implemented, which activity should be undertaken first?
n: A site survey (boundary, topographic and existing features) must come first. All site development planning depends on it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (site development plans based on survey); 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201 (site analysis).

q: This analytical problem-seeking process will lead to the statement and identification of both horizontal and vertical requirements in offering a solution. It incorporates a space program with characterizations of the envisioned spaces such as ambiance, cost range, etc.
n: Architectural programming is the analytical, problem-seeking process that states the horizontal and vertical requirements of a project. It includes a space program describing each space's ambiance, cost range and so on. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Architectural Programming.

q: Under which provision in RA 9266 do board passers automatically become members of the UAP as the IAPOA?
n: Section 40 integrates the profession into one national organization, the IAPOA (the UAP). Licensees automatically become members on registration. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40 (Integration of the Architecture Profession).

q: Under Section 15 of RA 9266 on Rating in the Licensure Examination, to be qualified as having passed the Licensure Examination for Architects, a candidate must obtain a weighted general average of how many percent, with no grade lower than 50% in any given subject?
n: To pass, a candidate needs a weighted general average of 70% with no grade below 50% in any subject. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 15 (Rating in the Licensure Examination).

q: Which section in RA 9266 provides for the ownership of plans, specifications and other contract documents duly signed, stamped or sealed, as instruments of service, as the intellectual property and documents of the architect?
n: Section 33 makes signed and sealed drawings, specifications and contract documents, as instruments of service, the intellectual property and documents of the architect. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33 (Ownership of Plans, Specifications and Other Contract Documents).

q: The provision on CPD can be found in which section of RA 9266?
n: Continuing Professional Development is provided under Section 28 of RA 9266. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 28 (Continuing Professional Development).

q: In the Philippine architecture profession, registered and licensed architects are required to engage in ongoing learning activities such as seminars, training programs, workshops, and professional development courses to maintain, update, and enhance their competencies. These activities fall under a mandatory program administered by the PRC. What does the acronym CPD stand for?
n: CPD stands for Continuing Professional Development, the PRC-mandated program of learning activities that licensed professionals must complete. Source: RA 10912 (CPD Act of 2016); RA 9266, Sec. 28.

q: Which section in RA 9266 states that the architecture profession shall be integrated into one (1) national organization which shall be accredited by the Board, subject to the approval of the Commission, as the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects?
n: Section 40 provides that the profession be integrated into one national organization accredited by the Board and approved by the Commission as the IAPOA. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40.

q: An apprentice has spent most of his apprenticeship performing only one type of architectural work. Upon reviewing his DAE Logbook, he realizes that although he has accumulated sufficient hours, he may not obtain the required experience credits in other fields of practice needed to qualify for the Licensure Examination for Architects. What should the apprentice do?
o: Monitor and regularly review his DAE Logbook and coordinate with his mentor or employer to obtain exposure in the deficient fields of practice.

Focus only on the field in which he has the greatest experience because R.A. No. 9266 recognizes specialization in architectural practice and such specialization is considered equivalent to diversified architectural experience.
Submit the DAE Logbook as is and request the PRBoA to waive any deficiencies in the lacking experience categories.
Continue accumulating additional hours in the same field because total experience hours are more important than diversified experience.
n: Diversified Architectural Experience requires credits across several fields of practice, not just hours in one. The apprentice should monitor the logbook and work with the mentor or employer to get exposure in the missing fields. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13 (qualifications: diversified architectural experience); PRBOA DAE guidelines.

q: Under R.A. No. 9266, under what condition may a foreign citizen be allowed to take the Licensure Examination for Architects in the Philippines?
o: When the foreign citizen's country allows Filipino architects to take their licensure examination and practice architecture on the same basis as its own citizens, subject to reciprocity.
Upon endorsement by the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture and the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects.
Upon establishing residence in the Philippines, graduating from a CHED-recognized school of architecture, and completing the required Diversified Architectural Experience (DAE).
Upon securing a valid work permit and being employed by a Philippine architectural firm.
n: A foreign citizen may take the exam only by reciprocity, when his or her country admits Filipino architects to its exam and practice on the same basis as its own citizens. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27 (Reciprocity Requirements).

q: It refers to the intellectual proprietary rights retained by an architect over any architectural document/work that he/she prepares unless there is a written stipulation to the contrary.
n: Copyright is the intellectual property right the architect keeps over any document or work he or she prepares, unless a written agreement says otherwise. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33; RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code), Sec. 172.

q: Under RA 9266, drawings, specifications, and other contract documents that are signed, stamped, or sealed as instruments of service are considered the intellectual property of whom?
n: Signed and sealed drawings, specifications and contract documents are instruments of service and the intellectual property of the architect. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33.

q: A type of bond that ensures that the contractor will complete the project in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract. It also guarantees that the contractor will pay all subcontractors, laborers and suppliers involved in the project.
n: A performance bond guarantees the contractor will complete the work according to the contract terms. Payment to subcontractors, laborers and suppliers is often bundled with it. Source: CIAP Document 102 (UGCC), Contract Bonds.

q: A type of bond that covers the quality of workmanship, materials installed and warranty of equipment that are part of the delivered project.
n: A guarantee (warranty) bond covers the quality of workmanship and materials and the warranty of installed equipment after the project is delivered. Source: CIAP Document 102 (UGCC), Guarantee Bond.

q: Most likely outcome for failure to complete the project on time
n: When the contractor fails to finish on time, liquidated damages for each day of delay are deducted as the contract stipulates. Source: CIAP Document 102 (UGCC), Liquidated Damages; Civil Code, Art. 2226.

q: When is the Guarantee Bond submitted by the contractor to the Architect?
n: The guarantee bond is posted after construction, at turnover and before final payment and release of retention. It covers the warranty period. Source: CIAP Document 102 (UGCC), Guarantee Bond.

q: Exits in parking structures shall be so arranged that no point in the area will be more than ___ from the nearest exit other than a ramp on the same floor level.
n: In parking structures, no point may be more than 45 m from the nearest exit other than a ramp on the same level. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Sec. 10.2.18.3.B.2.a.

q: Travel distance to exits in an enclosed parking structure may be increased to ___ if it is completely protected by an approved, supervised sprinkler system.
n: In enclosed parking structures fully protected by an approved, supervised sprinkler system, travel distance may increase to 60 m. Open floors of open parking structures allow 91 m. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Sec. 10.2.18.3.B.2.a, Exception No. 2.

q: During a fire safety inspection at a sports complex function hall in Manila, the BFP inspector measures the travel distance from the farthest occupied point of the hall to the nearest exit. The hall is not equipped with an approved, supervised sprinkler system. According to the Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514), what is the maximum allowable travel distance for this type of assembly occupancy?
n: In a place of assembly without an approved, supervised sprinkler system, travel to an exit may not exceed 46 m. The limit is 61 m with sprinklers. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Places of Assembly, Travel Distance to Exits.

q: In buildings without a sprinkler system, what is the maximum allowable line of travel from any point to the nearest exit, considering the stricter provision of the National Building Code of the Philippines?
n: The NBC allows 45.00 m to an exit in an unsprinklered building (60.00 m with sprinklers), stricter than the Fire Code's 46 m for assembly. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.2.d.

q: Exits shall be so arranged that at least two (2) separate exits will be available from every floor area. Exits shall be as remote from each other as practicable, so that there will be no pockets or dead ends in which occupants may be trapped, and in no case shall any dead-end corridor extend more than how many meters beyond the stairway or other means of exit therefrom?
n: No dead-end corridor may extend more than 6 m beyond the stairway or other exit. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Educational Occupancies, Exit Arrangement.

q: According to the National Building Code of the Philippines (only), what is the minimum required width for a corridor or exit balcony?
n: Every corridor or exterior exit balcony must be at least 1.10 m wide. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.4.a.

q: It is a continuous and unobstructed route of exit from one point in a building, structure or facility to a public way
n: A means of egress is a continuous, unobstructed route of exit from any point in a building to a public way. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Definition of Terms.

q: Minimum width of Means of Egress in mm
n: No means of egress may be narrower than 915 mm unless an occupancy chapter provides otherwise. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Sec. 10.2.5.2 (width of means of egress).

q: Minimum clear width of fire escape stairs in cm
n: Fire escape stairs need at least 600 mm (60 cm) clear between rails. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Table 6 (Dimensional Criteria for Fire Escape Stairs).

q: Minimum tread in cm of Fire Escape Stairs as per Fire Code of the Philippines
n: The minimum tread of a fire escape stair, excluding nosing, is 230 mm (23 cm). Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Table 6.

q: Maximum rise of Fire Escape Stairs in cm as per Fire Code of the Philippines
n: The maximum rise of a fire escape stair is 230 mm (23 cm). Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Table 6.

q: An abutment may be allowed for R-1 provided that it is used SOLELY for the purpose of supporting a carport roof, and provided further that it is constructed of PERFORATED or DECORATIVE material above 1.5 m measured vertically from the established grade level. How high can this abutment be?
n: In R-1, an abutment of up to 3.20 m above grade may be allowed only to support a carport roof. It must be perforated or decorative above 1.50 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704 (R-1 abutment exception).

q: Which residential zoning classification explicitly allows abutments only on one (1) side of the property line, and prohibits firewalls or abutments on both the front and rear property lines?
n: R-2 lots may have abutments on only one side. Firewalls or abutments are not allowed on the front and rear property lines. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 803 (abutments for basic uses), item ii.

q: According to the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the National Building Code of the Philippines, what is the only permitted exception to the absolute prohibition of window openings on, at, within, or through abutments erected along property lines such as firewalls?
n: No openings at all are allowed on or through abutments such as firewalls on property lines, except permitted vent wells. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 808.4.

q: Under socialized housing, the minimum lot frontage for a row house is
n: Under BP 220, row house lots need a minimum frontage of 4 m (economic) or 3.5 m (socialized). Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Minimum Lot Frontage table.

q: Under BP 220, what is the maximum number of dwelling units allowed per block or cluster in a row house development, provided the total length does not exceed 100 meters?
n: Row houses are limited to 20 units per block or cluster, and never more than 100 m long. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Minimum Lot Frontage notes; definition of Row House.

q: For subdivision projects with an area of one (1) hectare or more, the owner or developer shall reserve how many percent of the land area for open space?
n: Under PD 957, subdivision projects of one hectare or more must reserve 30% of the gross area for open space, including roads, parks and community facilities. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (2008), Sec. 5, Land Allocation.

q: A survey to establish the boundaries of a parcel using its legal description, which typically involves the setting or restoration of monuments or markers at the corners or along the lines of the parcel.
n: A boundary survey establishes a parcel's boundaries from its legal description, often setting or restoring monuments at the corners and along the lines. Source: DENR Manual for Land Surveys in the Philippines (DAO 2007-29), types of surveys.

q: A type of survey performed to re-establish the boundaries of a property by locating and verifying the original boundary markers or replacing them if they are missing or displaced. It ensures that the property boundaries align with the technical descriptions in the land title or survey plan.
n: A relocation survey re-establishes boundaries by finding and verifying the original markers, or replacing missing ones, to match the technical description in the title. Source: DENR Manual for Land Surveys in the Philippines (DAO 2007-29), relocation surveys.

q: A type of survey that maps the natural and artificial features of the land. It provides detailed information about the contours, elevations, vegetation, water bodies, structures and other characteristics of the land, giving a comprehensive understanding of the terrain which is vital for site development.
n: A topographic survey maps natural and man-made features such as contours, elevations, vegetation, water bodies and structures. It is the basis for site development. Source: DENR Manual for Land Surveys in the Philippines; NBC IRR Rule III (site development plans).

q: A type of survey which helps to determine precise locations, elevations, and dimensions for project features like structures, roads and utilities. The survey crew will take the proposed information depicted on the approved plans and place markers in order to relate them to the actual location on the particular property. This type of survey helps ensure accuracy during the building process, and it helps the architecture and engineering teams implement their designs and specifications in line with legal requirements.
n: A construction (layout or stake-out) survey places markers on site from the approved plans. This fixes the exact location, elevation and dimensions of structures, roads and utilities during building. Source: DENR Manual for Land Surveys in the Philippines; surveying practice (construction stake-out).

q: A type of survey that extensively evaluates subsurface utilities and structures to establish the location of telecommunications, gas, sewage, drainage pipes, fiber optics, water and others. It makes sure that these are preserved and not damaged during repair and construction works.
n: A utility survey locates underground utilities (telecom, gas, sewer, drainage, fiber optics, water) so they are not damaged during construction or repair. Source: Surveying practice (subsurface utility survey); NBC IRR Rule XI (protection of existing utilities).

q: Who signs and seals the survey plan?
n: Survey plans are signed and sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer. Source: RA 8560 (Philippine Geodetic Engineering Act of 1998), Sec. 4.
